title: MarketFoundry: Financial Knowledge Graph Pipeline
hook: Earnings transcripts and SEC filings hold the real signal, but it's buried. I built a pipeline that reads financial documents and turns them into queryable knowledge graphs. It extracted 5.2× more facts than Gemini using a 4B parameter model.
description: Market Foundry is a modular pipeline that transforms raw financial documents into queryable knowledge graphs. A stacked ensemble classifier (TF-IDF + KNN) routes documents across five types, LLM-powered topic extraction generates document-specific YAML schemas, and OneKE's multi-agent system extracts structured triples into Neo4j. Benchmarked against Gemini 3 Flash and Sonnet 4.6 on a Capital One SEC 8-K, Market Foundry extracted 5.2× more triples than Gemini and 2.1× more than Sonnet, with 3× the relation type diversity, using only a 4B parameter model. It was the only system to capture document-internal structure like linking exhibit numbers to merger agreements.
result: Impact: 5.2× more triples than Gemini 3 Flash, 2.1× more than Sonnet 4.6, and 3× more unique relation types, all from a 4B parameter model. 964 unique entities and 423 relationship types extracted across 112 documents.
alt: Market Foundry pipeline diagram showing document classification, topic extraction, schema-guided knowledge extraction, and Neo4j knowledge graph construction from financial documents

title: FlowScore: Cash Flow Credit Scoring Engine
hook: 76 million Americans are locked out of credit. The data trail needed to evaluate them simply does not exist. I built a cash flow underwriting engine to test whether transaction history could fill the gap.
description: FlowScore is a full cash flow underwriting pipeline: fine-tuned DistilBERT classifies 3.3M bank transactions into 21 categories, 45 behavioral features capture income stability, spending patterns, and obligation ratios, and a CatBoost model achieves 0.764 AUC, 11.2% above traditional scoring alone. The sharpest result is the fairness finding: thin-file borrowers are approved at 94.8% under FlowScore versus 3.2% by traditional scoring, a 29.4x gap that makes the access problem concrete.
result: Impact: 30.4% reduction in default losses at 70% approval; thin-file consumers approved 29.4x more often than under traditional scoring
alt: FlowScore dashboard comparing approval rates between traditional credit scoring and cash flow underwriting, highlighting a 29.4x improvement for thin-file borrowers

title: Payment Risk Insight Platform
hook: Every transaction: approve, review, or block, decided in milliseconds. I built a network-scale risk decisioning engine and proved the optimal policy captures 81.5% of fraud while maintaining 89.8% approval rates.
description: This project simulates a network-scale risk decisioning system that translates model scores into concrete policy actions. The pipeline defines approval thresholds, evaluates precision-recall tradeoffs under time-aware testing, and quantifies the economic cost of each policy choice in terms of fraud loss and customer friction.
result: Impact: Identified an optimal network policy capturing 81.5% of fraudulent activity while maintaining 89.8% approval rates, maximizing net economic value under realistic operational constraints.
alt: Payment Risk Insight Platform dashboard showing transaction risk scores, approval thresholds, and precision-recall tradeoff curves for fraud detection policy optimization

title: Market Digest: Automated News Intelligence
hook: 44% of AI-generated financial news claims were fabrications. I measured it, then engineered the architecture that brought accuracy to 98%.
description: Market Digest is a fully automated daily intelligence pipeline that scrapes 18 global sources, generates three-tier summaries across 7 verticals, and lets users query the news directly via RAG. The accuracy problem was the core challenge: only 44% of LLM-generated claims were supported by source articles. The fix was a negative-constraint prompt architecture that explicitly defines failure modes ('never speculate', 'never advise') alongside positive instructions, pushing accuracy from 44% to 98%. Every line of code was written by Claude Opus 4.6 as my coding agent, and a GitHub Actions pipeline runs the whole system autonomously every morning.
result: Impact: +54 percentage point improvement in claim accuracy (44% → 98%) through prompt engineering. 0.8s TTFT, 18 sources, 7 topics, 40s full bot execution in GitHub Actions CI; fully autonomous since day one.
alt: Market Digest app interface showing automated financial news summaries across 7 verticals and a RAG-powered chat window for querying the day's news

title: Wallet Risk & Behavior Analytics
hook: New crypto wallet, zero history. How do you tell a VIP from a fraudster? I clustered 1.2M Ethereum wallets and built the model that answers that in real time.
description: This project combines unsupervised wallet clustering (1.2M Ethereum wallets in BigQuery) with a supervised fraud model (XGBoost on the ETFD dataset) to answer two questions: what kind of wallet is this, and when should we intervene? The pipeline runs from segmentation through precision-recall tradeoffs to a cost model that converts fraud risk into concrete dollar figures.
result: Impact: ~75% reduction in simulated fraud loss by converting theft risk into a smaller, predictable support cost using behavior-only features.
alt: Crypto wallet analytics dashboard showing Ethereum wallet behavior clusters, XGBoost fraud scores, and cost-model breakdown of fraud loss versus support intervention

title: Trading Operations Reconciliation Engine
hook: A mismatch between the broker's records and the internal book carries direct financial liability. I built the surveillance system that catches it in under 15 seconds.
description: This project is a T+0 reconciliation engine built to catch the 'Break' problem: execution discrepancies in fees, prices, and phantom fills before the trading day ends. Optimized PostgreSQL bulk loads and Anti-Join verification logic bring time-to-detection from hours to seconds, converting manual fire-fighting into automated surveillance.
result: Impact: Achieved <15s runtime for 50k+ daily trades and 100% detection of simulated breaks, ensuring books are settlement-ready by market close.
alt: Trading Operations Reconciliation Engine dashboard showing real-time break detection results for 50,000+ daily trades, with anti-join verification and settlement status

title: VibeRecommender: Mood-First Audio Engine
hook: Stop saying 'chill pop.' Tell your music app exactly what you want: high-energy, low-speech, mid-tempo. I built the 7-dimensional engine that actually understands that.
description: Vibe Recommender is a content-based music recommendation engine built around 7 audio features. It offers three interaction modes: sliders for precise feature control, seed-from-song for audio-grounded recommendations, and Vibe Roulette, a time-of-day persona that auto-generates a playlist based on the current hour. The goal was a listening surface that responds to how you actually describe music, not just genre labels.
result: Feature: 'Vibe Roulette' uses datetime logic to automate context-aware playlists.
alt: VibeRecommender interface showing 7-dimensional audio feature sliders for energy, tempo, and acousticness, alongside mood-based music recommendations

title: Forecasting Volatility: The BERT vs. FinBERT Experiment
hook: The finance-specialized model was supposed to win. It did not, and the reason reshapes how you should think about domain expertise in AI.
description: We fine-tuned both BERT and FinBERT to classify short-term stock volatility from financial headlines, then measured the results. The financial-specific model developed a severe Optimism Bias: high recall, low precision, aggressively predicting growth even during downturns. The generic BERT was the better risk manager, filtering noise to deliver superior risk-adjusted returns.
result: Discovery: Falsified the domain-superiority hypothesis. Generic BERT beat the specialized model in stability (Sharpe 0.010) by minimizing false positives.
alt: Animated visualization comparing BERT and FinBERT classification performance on financial headlines, showing FinBERT's optimism bias versus BERT's more conservative volatility predictions

title: The Commitment Engine: Predicting Non-Refundable Playtime
hook: On Steam, a sale followed by a refund is a lost transaction. Most recommenders optimize for clicks. We built the model that optimizes for commitment, and it knew the difference.
description: We built a prediction engine targeting 'Commitment' rather than clicks: purchases that clear the 2-hour threshold and never get refunded. The key design decision was Hybrid Negative Sampling, feeding the model both Soft Negatives (random unowned games) and Hard Negatives (abandoned purchases) so it could learn the difference between a future favorite and a case of buyer's regret.
result: Outcome: Processed 5.15M interactions to achieve 0.88 AUC, successfully predicting refund-proof engagement.
alt: Steam game commitment prediction model showing hybrid negative sampling pipeline architecture and precision-recall optimization results across 5.15 million user interactions

title: Neural Earth: Hybrid Climate Emulation
hook: Physics-based climate models take hours per simulation. I got it down to seconds with a neural architecture that generalizes to scenarios it has never seen.
description: I engineered a Hybrid U-Net + FNO architecture that combines U-Net's local feature extraction with the Fourier Neural Operator's global spectral processing. To train this deep, memory-intensive model on limited compute, I implemented Mixed-Precision (FP16) training and custom gradient clipping, enabling 100-year climate projections in seconds.
result: Performance: Achieved 1.31 RMSE on unseen future scenarios (SSP245), ranking in the Top 25% of the competition.
alt: Neural Earth climate emulation model output showing U-Net FNO hybrid architecture predictions for 100-year global temperature and precipitation scenarios under SSP245

title: XGBoost Algorithmic Trading
hook: What if technical analysis could be systematized? I replaced chart-reading intuition with 15 engineered signals and a model that only bets when the edge is real. Sharpe 3.82.
description: I engineered an automated trading system that streams market data via the yfinance API and calculates 15+ technical indicators (RSI, MACD, Volatility). XGBoost classifies short-term price direction, and trades execute only when confidence clears a high-probability threshold, keeping capital concentrated on the clearest signals.
result: Performance: Achieved a 3.82 Sharpe Ratio and significant alpha over Buy & Hold in historical simulations.
alt: XGBoost algorithmic trading system chart showing technical indicator signals, predicted price direction, and backtested performance versus buy-and-hold benchmark

title: Visualizing Algorithmic Bias in Healthcare
hook: An algorithm was denying care to Asian women at a 79% higher rate. Nobody knew because nobody looked. We built the tool that made it impossible to ignore.
description: We built an interactive dashboard exposing how opioid prescription algorithms disproportionately deny care to Asian women. The project uses real-world medical datasets to visualize approval rates by race and gender, making the disparity concrete and hard to dismiss.
result: Finding: Visualized a 79% denial rate disparity using real-world medical datasets.
alt: Interactive heatmap dashboard showing opioid prescription denial rates segmented by race and gender, exposing a 79% disparity against Asian women in algorithmic decision-making

title: Real-Time Robotics Classification
hook: No labeled dataset? No problem. I scraped one from scratch, then used transfer learning to build a real-time classifier that tells drones from rovers from robotic arms.
description: I scraped a custom dataset from scratch and applied Transfer Learning with MobileNetV2 to train a lightweight classifier that distinguishes drones, rovers, and robotic arms in real time. The project was constrained by limited labeled data, which MobileNetV2's pretrained feature extraction was well-suited to handle.
result: Metrics: 56% Improved Accuracy on custom scraped dataset.
alt: Real-time robotics classification architecture diagram showing MobileNetV2 transfer learning pipeline for distinguishing drones, rovers, and robotic arms from a custom scraped dataset

title: Quantifying the 'Home Court' Advantage
hook: Does the 12th Man actually move the needle? I ran the numbers on 20,000+ games to find out. The answer is statistically significant.
description: We ran a deep statistical analysis of 20,000+ NBA and NFL games, measuring how home crowd presence affects point differentials. The work covers psychological and statistical dimensions, testing whether the effect holds up to formal significance testing across two major sports.
result: Result: Confirmed statistical significance (p < 0.001) of crowd impact on game outcomes.
alt: Statistical visualization of NBA and NFL home court advantage analysis across 20,000+ games, showing crowd impact on point differentials with p-value significance testing
